title: How long would it take you?
subtopic: T1 — the question, and today's answers
learning_goal: Know that a full circumnavigation now takes about 44 hours by scheduled flight and 90 minutes in orbit, and that in 1872 nobody knew the answer at all.

narration.script: How long would it take you to go all the way round the world? Today, about forty-four hours. In November twenty twenty-four, three men from Hong Kong went the whole way round on ordinary scheduled flights, on tickets anyone could buy. Higher up it is faster. The space station laps the planet every ninety minutes. The people on board watch sixteen sunrises a day. Now take all of that away. No aircraft. No radio. In eighteen seventy-two the honest answer was: nobody knew. So somebody turned it into a bet. Eighty days, half a fortune — and for the next hundred and fifty years, real people kept trying to beat him.

T1.3 — the comparison card, built one line at a time: 90 MINUTES / 44 HOURS 33 MINUTES / 80 DAYS. Three lines, nothing else. Type large enough to read on a phone. The guide does not read the numbers the card shows. ESSENTIAL, DOES NOT EXIST YET. 2026-09-11: all three lines up within about a second. With no beats the card built them evenly across the slot, so the voice said '80 days' while only '90 minutes' was on screen.
